user.title: Add VIGI or InSight Camera
user.description: Enter the camera's local IP address and credentials.

name.title: Name this camera
name.description: The name pulled from the camera is shown below. This names the integration entry. The device and its entity IDs use the name set on the camera itself — to change those, rename the device in Home Assistant afterwards.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate camera
reauth_confirm.description:
Home Assistant could not sign in to **{name}** at `{host}` with the stored credentials.

This usually means the camera's password was changed. Enter the current one below — the camera keeps its existing entities, history and automations.

Use the camera's **local** admin password, not your TP-Link ID / VIGI cloud account password.

If `{host}` is no longer this camera's address, close this and add the camera again at its new address instead — see *My camera's IP address changed* under Troubleshooting on the integration's GitHub page.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to camera — check the IP address and ensure the camera is reachable.

abort.already_configured: This camera is already set up in Home Assistant (recognised by its MAC address). Nothing was changed; if it had failed to set up, it is being retried now.
abort.reauth_successful: Credentials updated. The camera is reconnecting and its entities will return in a few seconds.
abort.reauth_entry_gone: This camera is no longer configured in Home Assistant, so there is nothing to re-authenticate.
abort.wrong_camera: Those credentials reached a different camera than the one this entry was set up for — its IP address has most likely been reassigned. Close this, find the camera's current address (your router's client list or the VIGI app), then use Add Integration → VIGI & InSight Cameras with that address. Do not delete the existing camera first: Home Assistant will recognise it and move the existing entry to the new address, keeping its entities.
abort.host_updated: This camera is already set up (recognised by its MAC address), so the existing entry has been updated with the address and password you entered and is reconnecting. Its entities, history and automations are unchanged.

init.title: Camera feature groups

data.feature_detection_events: Detection events (motion, person, intrusion, and other binary sensors)
data.feature_image_controls: Image controls (brightness, contrast, WDR, flip, and other camera tuning — disabled by default)

data_description.feature_camera_stream:
Detected: {capabilities}

Disable if Frigate or another integration already provides the camera stream.
data_description.stream_use_main:
When off (default), the sub-stream (stream2) is used for live view — lower resolution but fast startup and smooth playback on Raspberry Pi and other low-powered hardware.

When on, the main HD stream (stream1) is used — full resolution but requires more CPU and network headroom to transcode without buffering. Recommended only on more powerful hardware.
data_description.feature_detection_events: {note}Disable if Frigate handles detection — this also stops ONVIF event subscriptions.
data_description.feature_image_controls: Adds camera tuning controls to the Configuration section of the device. Entities are disabled by default — enable them individually from the device page. Most users leave this off.

sd_card_missing.title: SD card no longer detected — {camera_name}
sd_card_missing.description:
The SD card was previously present in **{camera_name}** but is no longer detected. SD card sensor entities are still in Home Assistant.

If you have removed the card temporarily, dismiss this — the entities will keep working once the card is reinserted.

If you are no longer using an SD card in this camera, delete the unwanted SD card entities from the device page, then dismiss this notice.

frigate_camera_gone.title: Frigate camera link lost — {camera_name}
frigate_camera_gone.description:
**{camera_name}** was previously detected alongside a Frigate camera at this IP address, but Frigate no longer has a camera here.

If Frigate was removed or reconfigured, you may want to re-enable **Camera Stream** and **Detection Events** for this camera:
1. Go to **Settings → Devices & Services → VIGI & InSight Cameras**
2. Select **{camera_name} → Configure**
3. Re-enable the relevant feature groups

Dismiss this notice once you have decided how to proceed.

wrong_camera_at_address.title: {title} has moved: a different camera is at {host}
wrong_camera_at_address.description:
**{title}** is set up at `{host}`, but a different camera is answering there now — most likely your router gave the cameras new addresses, for example after a power cut. To avoid acting on the wrong camera, VIGICam has stopped controlling **{title}** until this is fixed.

1. Find **{title}**'s current address: look for MAC address `{mac}` in your router's client list, or check the VIGI app.
2. Go to **Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → VIGI & InSight Cameras** and enter that address with the camera's username and password. Do **not** delete the existing camera first — Home Assistant recognises it, moves it to the new address and keeps its entities and history.
3. If more than one camera shows this notice, repeat for each.

This notice clears itself once the right camera answers. Giving each camera a fixed address (a DHCP reservation in your router) stops it happening again.

If you **replaced** {title} with a new camera at the same address, delete {title} and add the new camera instead — give it the same name to keep the same entity IDs.
